findings.title: Division by zero in percent change calculation
findings.description: In economic-chart-card.tsx, the percentChange calculation divides by prev.value without checking if it's zero. If the previous data point has a value of 0, this will result in Infinity or NaN being displayed in the UI.
findings.suggested_issue: Add a guard clause to check if prev.value is zero before calculating percentChange. Return null or 0 when prev.value is 0 to prevent division by zero.

findings.title: Division by zero in diffFromAvg calculation
findings.description: In economic-chart-card.tsx, the diffFromAvg calculation divides by avg without checking if it's zero. If all values in the series are 0, the average will be 0, causing division by zero.
findings.suggested_issue: Add a guard clause to check if avg is zero before calculating diffFromAvg. Return 0 or skip the insight generation when avg is 0.

findings.title: Missing null check for series[0] before accessing config
findings.description: In economic-chart-card.tsx stats calculation, series[0] is accessed after checking seriesList.length but the series array itself could have undefined elements if the array is sparse.
findings.snippet:
if (!seriesList.length || !series[0]) return null;
const config = series[0];
findings.suggested_issue: The check is present but could be more defensive. Consider using optional chaining when accessing config properties downstream.

findings.title: Potential race condition in unit override logic
findings.description: In useEconomicData.ts, the unit assignment logic has multiple conditional branches that can lead to inconsistent unit values when points arrive in different orders. The group.unit can be overwritten mid-iteration.
findings.suggested_issue: Establish a clear priority for unit sources (pointUnit > defaultUnit > existing) and apply it consistently. Consider using the first non-null unit encountered rather than overwriting.

findings.title: parseDate falls back to current date silently
findings.description: In akshare.service.ts, parseDate returns new Date() when parsing fails. This silently inserts current timestamps for invalid data, corrupting time series data without any warning or error.
findings.suggested_issue: Instead of silently returning current date, either throw an error, return null and filter out invalid points, or log a warning. Silent fallback to current date corrupts historical data.

findings.title: parseYearMonthDate falls back to current date silently
findings.description: In akshare.service.ts, parseYearMonthDate returns new Date() when year/month parsing fails. This can silently corrupt time series data by inserting current timestamps for invalid records.
findings.suggested_issue: Return null instead of current date and filter out points with null dates in the calling parser methods. Log a warning when date parsing fails.

findings.title: Aggregation loses data type and unit information
findings.description: In akshare.service.ts getDataByCategory, when granularity bucketing is applied, the aggregation uses the first sample's metadata for all aggregated points. If different sourceFields have different units or dataTypes, this information is lost.
findings.snippet: const bucketed = new Map<string, { timestamp: Date; valueSum: number; count: number; sample: typeof points[number] }>();
findings.suggested_issue: Bucket by both timestamp AND sourceField to preserve per-field aggregation. Alternatively, validate that all points in a bucket have the same unit/dataType before aggregating.

findings.title: Empty chart option returned without proper structure
findings.description: In global-sentiment-trend.tsx, when data is empty or undefined, an empty object {} is returned as the chart option. This may cause ECharts to render incorrectly or throw errors depending on the chart component implementation.
findings.suggested_issue: Return a properly structured empty chart option with at least xAxis, yAxis, and empty series array to prevent potential rendering issues.

findings.title: GraphQL resolver returns undefined for optional fields without explicit null
findings.description: In economic-data.resolver.ts, optional fields like groupLabel, lastRunAt, lastStatus use ?? undefined which may cause GraphQL serialization issues. GraphQL expects explicit null for nullable fields, not undefined.
findings.suggested_issue: Use ?? null instead of ?? undefined for GraphQL nullable fields to ensure proper serialization and client-side handling.

findings.title: calculatePercentChange returns null when base.value is 0
findings.description: In series.ts, calculatePercentChange correctly checks for base.value === 0 and returns null, but this edge case is not communicated to the UI. Components using this function may not handle null returns gracefully.
findings.suggested_issue: Document this behavior and ensure all UI components that call calculatePercentChange handle null returns with appropriate fallback display (e.g., 'N/A' or '--').

findings.title: Tooltip formatter may crash on malformed params
findings.description: In economic-chart-card.tsx buildOption, the tooltip formatter accesses params properties without defensive checks. If ECharts passes malformed params (e.g., during rapid updates or edge cases), this could throw.
findings.suggested_issue: Wrap the formatter logic in a try-catch block and return an empty string or fallback message on error to prevent chart crashes.

findings.title: Number conversion without validation in resolver
findings.description: In economic-data.resolver.ts, point.value is converted to Number without checking if the result is valid. Prisma Decimal values that are too large or malformed could result in NaN or Infinity.
findings.suggested_issue: Add validation after Number conversion: const numValue = Number(point.value); if (!Number.isFinite(numValue)) { /* handle error or skip */ }
